name: NAIF | Offline Webhook Signature and Retry Fixture Lab (Synthetic Only)

parameters.jsCode: const seen=new Set();return $input.all().map(item=>{ const x=item.json;let verdict;if(typeof x.supplied_signature!=="string"||x.supplied_signature.length===0){verdict="MISSING_SIGNATURE";}else if(!/^sha256=[a-f0-9]{64}$/.test(x.supplied_signature)||x.supplied_signature!=="sha256="+x.computed_hmac_hex){verdict="INVALID_SIGNATURE";}else if(!x.event_id||seen.has(x.event_id)){verdict="DUPLICATE_IN_THIS_BATCH";}else{seen.add(x.event_id);verdict="ACCEPTED_SYNTHETIC";}return {json:{label:x.label,verdict,event_id:x.event_id,demo_only:true}};});

parameters.content:
### How it works
This free offline demonstration explains two common webhook incidents: a signature that no longer matches the raw request body and an event sent more than once. Click Execute workflow manually. A fixture node creates four entirely synthetic requests: valid, altered body, missing signature, and duplicate. The native Crypto node calculates HMAC SHA256 for the exact synthetic text, a Code node classifies the cases, and the final Code node reports PASS or FAIL. The workflow never listens for real webhooks and makes no external requests.

### Setup
Import this workflow JSON into an isolated n8n editor. Create a new Crypto credential with its HMAC Secret set to the literal *public test string* NAIF-demo-test-key-DO-NOT-USE-IN-PRODUCTION. Select the credential in Calculate synthetic HMAC. Do not reuse that string in real systems. Click Execute workflow; verify four cases and one successful summary. No external service accounts or paid tools are needed. For a fresh-import check, export, re-import to a new workflow, set the demo credential there too, and run again.

### Customization
Change the synthetic raw-body text to see why even whitespace can invalidate a signature. The replay set exists only for the current run. Real receivers additionally require provider-specific signature headers, timestamps, constant-time comparison, secure secrets, bounded payloads, and persistent idempotency. This lab does not deliver or repair live webhooks.

## Synthetic input only
Manual Trigger creates four safe fixture cases. No real webhook receiver or provider API.

## Local HMAC checks
Use the native Crypto credential with the fake demo HMAC test string. Then classify and summarize each fixture.

**DEMO ONLY:** The example key is public. Replay detection resets on every run. This is not a provider-specific production webhook receiver, constant-time authenticator, or persistent deduplication system.
